items.title: [theglobeandmail.com] B.C. voters cast ballots in close race as officials hand-count votes
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

British Columbia voters are choosing a 93-member legislature Saturday in a snap provincial election called two years early, with the governing New Democratic Party (NDP) and the Conservative Party of B.C. running close in final polls. During the campaign, Premier David Eby acknowledged frustration over the early election call, while both major parties promoted competing plans on affordability, health care and the economy. Eby initially cited U.S. President Donald Trump’s trade threat as a reason to seek a new mandate, then said he should have explained more clearly that the legislature had stalled under the NDP’s narrow majority. Eby also accused interim Conservative leader Lorne Doerkson of serving as a “Trojan horse” for extremists in his party; Doerkson called that characterization “absurd”. Election officials will count election-day ballots by hand because the snap vote left Elections BC too little time to prepare enough tabulators. Officials will electronically tabulate advance-voting and electoral-office ballots and report those results first. Absentee and mail-in ballots will not be included in election-night totals; they are scheduled for the final count from Nov. 6 to Nov. 10.

items.title: [cnbc.com] Meta lifts AI spending plan as $825 billion commitments unsettle investors
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Meta Platforms shares fell nearly 7% on Thursday, Oct. 22, after the company raised the lower end of its 2026 capital-spending forecast by $5 billion and reported negative quarterly free cash flow for the first time in more than a decade. Meta also disclosed about $825 billion in future lease and contract commitments tied largely to its AI infrastructure buildout. Third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, beating analysts’ expectations, but free cash flow was negative $2.12 billion as spending increased. Meta said it plans to create nonvoting Class C shares to give it more flexibility to finance growth; it has said it could raise hundreds of billions of dollars over several years through share issuances. The selloff extended beyond Meta: the Nasdaq fell 2.6%, the S&P 500 lost 1.2% and the Philadelphia semiconductor index dropped about 6.7% on Thursday. Meta’s new share class is scheduled to take effect on Jan. 19, 2027, under the company’s plan.

items.title: [fortune.com] AI models uncover decades-old PHP flaws, heightening cyberattack risks
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Researchers at cybersecurity firm Calif used OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol model to find a critical flaw in PHP. Google-owned security company Wiz independently used Google’s Gemini 4 Argon and OpenAI models to identify vulnerabilities in the same core software. PHP maintainers released fixes on Oct. 21 for the two flaws, which had remained hidden for years and could let attackers run code on vulnerable servers without authentication. Wiz said frontier models made a complex exploit chain substantially easier to execute, describing steps that had once been at the edge of what human researchers could achieve. The same capabilities could help attackers adapt exploits to different PHP versions and server configurations, the company warned. OpenAI said it believes researchers found the flaws before attackers did. It is proposing a repeatable process for identifying and fixing vulnerabilities in widely used software and preparing defenses against them. The company said it expects similar discoveries to increase sharply in coming months.

items.title: [cbc.ca] Canadian police suspend use of Crime Stoppers after 1.5 million records exposed
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Canadian police services are suspending their use of Crime Stoppers after a breach exposed more than 1.5 million tips submitted across Canada over 25 years, a CBC News investigation found. More than 850,000 records included personally identifiable information. The tips were managed through P3, software provided by U.S.-based Navigate360. Navigate360 acknowledged on Friday that its database had been breached between November 2025 and March 2026 and said potentially exposed information included names, addresses, birth dates and Social Security numbers. The company said it had no evidence the information had been used for fraud or identity theft. Police in several provinces have paused their use of the service while they assess the breach and its safeguards. Toronto and Ottawa police are directing people to report information through police channels, which do not necessarily offer the same anonymity. Crime Stoppers chapters and police are seeking further details from Navigate360. The company said it hired a cybersecurity firm to help strengthen security.

🏔️ ✏️

Canada’s federal government said it is assessing President Donald Trump’s Oct. 23 order changing which Canadian goods face U.S. tariffs, as Ottawa seeks a broader trade arrangement. The order removes 50% duties on some Canadian exports but adds other goods to the tariff list. The changes take effect Oct. 30. Canada’s trade minister, Dominic LeBlanc, said Ottawa remained ready to work in good faith toward a trade relationship that respects Canadian interests. Prime Minister Mark Carney, speaking in Turkey, said Canada would not rush into a deal and would wait for acceptable terms. Substantive negotiations have been stalled since talks broke down in August. Derek Nighbor, president of the Forest Products Association of Canada, said lumber, furniture and kitchen cabinetry remain subject to U.S. duties. The Canadian Federation of Agriculture called for the removal of all recently imposed tariffs and agriculture-related retaliatory measures.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Herdade da Matinha Country House / Sabrab
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Between the cork oaks and the Vicentina Coast, Herdade da Matinha was born from an abandoned Alentejo estate, whose chimney still bears the date 1917. This rural tourism project, developed by SABRAB Architecture in collaboration with the owner Alfredo Moreira da Silva, starts from a simple principle: to make use of what already existed and add only what was necessary, with the same economy of means that has always characterized rural construction in the Alentejo region.
